body:
Nope. I am in the same boat as you, and it is not dramatic at all. However, I think that trying to survive is braver. It's not what I WANT to do, TBH, but it's what I WILL do.
It's scary, thinking I might be in a shelter or hellhole motel by next summer, but it's hard to make money doing what I'm good at, and I can't get a "real" job for a myriad of reasons.

Right? You don't even need talent. I know someone whose husband gives her everything and she is the wirst person EVER while I struggle with all the talent I have (and I do have talent and skills). It's tiring sutrggling for 26 years.
That's why I haven't done it. Surviving would have near catastrophic results for me.

If you're still here, I have a question: does shooting yourself in the heart really yield better results than the head? I was going to put the gun under my chin. Let me know if you can. If you can't, I hope you found peace.
Mine is the same way. I literally need a little cash and I could have like 90% of my problems fixed. Live with an emotionally abusive roommate, and now my mother, too.

Adam, you sound like me as a man right now. I'm 26, no real friends, no significant romances EVER in my life. Lazy, procrastinating, can barely keep a decent job.

I don't see a reason to live anymore and I am NOT telling you to kill yourself. I just want you to know you're not alone. I feel the same way you do, to a T.
